slideDifferences.nativeText:
Talking about the past can also have two main grammatical aspects to consider. To Be and other verbs.
TO CONSIDER

Even in past, the verb to be is an independent verb it can say a sentence, it can make a question or deny by itself. NO AUXILIARY NEEDED
IT has two forms in past: 
Was ( I/ He / She / It) 
            Were ( You / we / you/ They)
To Be verb
He was at home yesterday.
Was he at home yesterday?
They were in the school this morning.
Were they in the school this morning?
Other verbs – Auxiliary Introduction
John made a cake last night.
Did he make a cake last night?
I visited my family in Christmas.
Did you visit your family? / What did you do in Christmas?
TO CONSIDER
The rest of the verbs are dependent. They use the past auxiliary DID.
DID works for all the pronouns. 
Verbs go in simple form when DID is in the sentence. 
Verbs in past are divided into two groups: 
Regular: They follow a pattern. 
Irregular: They change. / They don’t Change.
Check out this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XulHb3KEQPs&list=PL6c5c6_b89gr7bHe6Zf-CUUp_zEHkJaJK&index=2

texts: Talking about the past can also have two main grammatical aspects to consider. To Be and other verbs.
Even in past, the verb to be is an independent verb it can say a sentence, it can make a question or deny by itself. NO AUXILIARY NEEDED
IT has two forms in past:
They were in the school this morning.
Were they in the school this morning?
John made a cake last night.
Did he make a cake last night?
I visited my family in Christmas.
Did you visit your family? / What did you do in Christmas?
The rest of the verbs are dependent. They use the past auxiliary DID.
DID works for all the pronouns.
Verbs go in simple form when DID is in the sentence.
Verbs in past are divided into two groups:
Irregular: They change. / They don’t Change.
